name: William Howitt
bio: William Howitt (1792–1879) was an English writer, born at Heanor in Derbyshire and brought up a Quaker. He wrote widely on country life, travel and history, and with his wife Mary Howitt produced many volumes of verse and prose.
His best-known poem is “The Departure of the Swallow”, a short lyric that Stedman placed among the English song writers in A Victorian Anthology (1895).

poems.title: The Departure of the Swallow
poems.author: William Howitt
poems.collection: A Victorian Anthology, 1837–1895, ed. Edmund Clarence Stedman (1895)
poems.text:
And is the swallow gone?
Who beheld it?
Which way sail'd it?
Farewell bade it none?

No mortal saw it go:
But who doth hear
Its summer cheer
As it flitteth to and fro?

So the freed spirit flies!
From its surrounding clay
It steals away
Like the swallow from the skies.

Whither? wherefore doth it go?
'Tis all unknown:
We feel alone
That a void is left below.
